title: the estate page's plan usage blanks on a 429, and intentd re-asks the endpoint every minute with no backoff
body:
hv, 2026-10-27, on the estate page's PLAN USAGE card, which read `usage endpoint failed: the endpoint answered 429. No fallback has reported either.` with every bar empty: "Any idea why this isn't working?" ic read the source and the host before answering.

WHAT WAS SEEN. The account's usage endpoint, `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage`, answered 429 to intentd's census read. It was refusing the account's token, not intentd alone: hv's Claude Usage menubar app reads the same URL with the same Keychain token, and a screenshot of it taken at 06:37:03Z (the file's UTC birth time) read "Updated 53 minutes ago" with its refresh spinner turning.

WHY THE CARD IS EMPTY, AND WHY intentd ADDS TO THE PRESSURE (intentd/src/census.rs, intentsvcs/src/estate/usage.rs). (1) A failed reading replaces the last good one: the tick keeps a failed `Endpoint` exactly as it keeps a good one, so one 429 blanks the card, where the menubar app keeps its last numbers and their age. (2) Every `/estate/status` read arms the next endpoint read, and the tick reads once a minute while anything asks, with no backoff and no reading of `Retry-After`, so a page left open re-asks a refusing endpoint every minute. (3) The statusline fallback has never reported on this host: `~/.local/state/intent/estate/` holds no `*.usage.json`, because hv's statusLine (`npx -y ccstatusline@2.0.12`) does not pipe its input to `intent estate statusline`. Wiring that is hv's settings.json, and it is outside this issue.

THE FIX (S; hv, in ic's session on 2026-10-27, "Ok, do 1 and 2.", on ic's offer; vc's three points of 07:04Z by vc's clock):
- `usage::carry`: a failed read after a good one keeps that reading, still stamped with its `read_at`, with the failure named in `usage.error`. A failure with nothing good behind it stays the failure, and a good read replaces whatever was kept. `usage::resolve` shows a kept reading unless a statusline report is newer, and then it shows the report, naming the same failure.
- `usage::next_wait`: while the estate is asked for, the census reads the endpoint at most every five minutes (`READ_EVERY`). After a failure it waits twice the previous wait, from five minutes up to an hour (`WAIT_CAP`), and never sooner than a 429's `Retry-After` in seconds. A 429 is its own failure, `EndpointFailure::Throttled { retry_after }`, read from curl's `-w "\n%{http_code} %header{retry-after}"`; every other status stays `Status { status }`.
- census.rs keeps the schedule in the tick: an ask that arrives before the read is due stays armed rather than spent.
- Files: native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/estate/usage.rs, native/rust/crates/intentd/src/census.rs, and native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/tests/the_usage_endpoint_names_each_failure.rs, AT-02.6's file, which gains the arms for the 429, the kept reading and the wait. shell.html is unchanged, because the card already draws a reading beside an error with its age.

IT CHANGES A SATISFIED CRITERION (vc). AC-02.6 reads "read by intentd once per census tick after a status ask". At landing, in the landing chain, `intent ac edit ST0086 AC-02.6` makes it "read by intentd on a census tick after a status ask, at most every five minutes, and after a failed read no sooner than twice the previous wait, up to an hour, or a 429's Retry-After", and the failure clause gains "and a failed read after a good one keeps that reading, with when it was read, beside the failure, until a newer statusline report replaces it". AT-02.6 is re-cited with its new arms. The failure naming AC-02.6 asks for stays; the kept reading adds to it and replaces nothing. ST0086 design.md's Primary paragraph ("at most once a census tick ... it keeps the last answer in memory") is corrected through the attachment door in the same landing.

BASE AND TRAIN. Banked over Part B's tree, cc's scratch tip e22661b78 (Part B's six banks over main 5d9b5e2be), so the train after Part B's stays one stack with 0657 and ST0081 WP-02. No Part B bank touches these files. Light work under the L1 hold: edits and git only, no build, no suite. No CHANGELOG hunk (decision 92); vc writes its line at landing.


VC'S READ OF v2 (2026-10-27, 08:34Z by vc's date -u). v1 (refs/bank/ic/0658/v1, blob 876b862b11c2) is withdrawn: its census.rs called `Instant::now`, which one_clock.rs bans outside the two files it exempts. v2 (refs/bank/ic/0658/v2, blob 29282d37ceb3, patch-id 3534a4ebafa3, banked over e22661b78 to tree 8fb60935efd9) keeps the schedule in whole census ticks with no clock read. It passes every mechanical check: the bank equals ic's worktree, one_clock's needles find nothing in it, its paths reach neither exit_code_consumers nor the dispatch table's populations, rustfmt passes, and the train stacks 0657 v2, ST0081 WP-02 v1 and 0658 v2 to tree 66c60d9bc8a7.

ONE FINDING, BY READING, NOT MEASURED. `ticks_to_wait`'s doc and AT-02.6's new unit arm promise a wait that is never short of `waited`, but a read made on a whole tick waits short by about the read's own duration. Its answer arrives some way into the tick, after the sample, the prune and curl (which MAX_TIME caps at 10 s), while the follow-up goes out a whole number of ticks after the tick itself. So every wait that is a whole number of minutes is short by that much: READ_EVERY, WAIT_CAP, their doublings, and a whole-minute Retry-After. v1 took its due time after the read and was never short.

v3 owes one of two fixes. vc recommends one more tick for every read (`div_ceil` plus one, with `whole` dropped from `ticks_to_wait`). The wait is then never short while the answer comes before the next tick, the steady cadence is six minutes, and AC-02.6's landing wording above holds as written. The alternative keeps the code and rewords the doc, the arm's name and AC-02.6's Retry-After clause to the true bound: short by at most the read's own duration. ic took the recommended fix for v3, and wrote that it counted from the tick the read began in, not from its answer, so an on-tick read lost its own curl time.
